links.note: The five statements to be explained from the text are the chapter's comprehension block, which this set holds as 31601. No single beat covers all five (they run from 31591 through 31598), so the exercise concept is the honest home.
At its best, at risk, at hand, at once, at all, at a low ebb and at first sight are 31603's own list.
Endure, persist, signify, confide, maintain and abhor taking -ance or -ence is the first half of 31602.
Matching remote, means, dominant, formidable and overwhelmed to their meanings and using them is the second half of 31602. 31603 is the at-phrases.

Humility while looking over the panorama belongs to the summit's overwhelming thankfulness in 31591. 31589 is the body's relief and 31590 the tinge of sadness - the two feelings this item is set against.
'Never the same again' is 31591's permanent change.
The other summit is the one in the mind, which is 31598. 31599 is that it cannot be climbed on anyone's behalf.
Becoming conscious of his own smallness follows straight from 'never the same again' in 31591.
Straining every nerve for another step is the brutal struggle with rock and ice in 31594. 31595 is the two-man rope work on the last heights.
Cursing yourself for letting yourself in for this is the same last-ounce-of-energy passage, 31594, which also notes the way back is as hard as the way on.
Telling yourself it was worthwhile closes the struggle passage of 31594. 31600 is the later judgement about the internal summit being worth as much.
The peaks like a jewelled necklace is the view at the end of that same final push, 31594. 31593 is the general beauty of mountains as a reason for climbing.
Bowing in submission at the peak is the reverence of 31597, the concept of the relics left there rather than of conquest.
That every man carries a peak within himself is 31598's own sentence.
Climbing it for fuller knowledge of who you are is 31599, which also says nobody can do it for you. 31598 only establishes that the inner peak exists.
That the climb certainly changes you is 31591. 31600 is what the change then equips him for.
He did not climb alone, and 31595 is why - on the last heights two climbers share one rope, one cutting steps and belaying while the other inches up. 31596 is the written record of help received.
Loving to rise on a summer morning is the poem's opening delight, 31604. NOTE: the stem prints 'sunday morn' where Blake has 'summer morn'.

The little ones spending the day in sighing and dismay is the school-misery section that 31605 describes, alongside the drooping child and the caged bird. 31604 is the morning outdoors that school takes away.
